title: Cross-Ledger Inventory Consistency (Conservation Across Networked Representations)

dascp.note: Formalizes the supply-conservation core of C51-N (sum of cross-ledger representations equals issued supply); the broader 'shared data' dimension of C51-N (reconciliation of non-supply data such as identity, transaction history) is intentionally not covered here — that is a separate cross-ledger data-consistency obligation that would need its own property.

descriptions.semantic: Across every ledger L_1, ..., L_n that holds a representation of asset a — native issuance on its home ledger plus any number of bridged / wrapped representations elsewhere — the sum of representations equals the asset's globally issued supply. That sum changes only via authorized bridge transfer protocols whose mint-on-destination and burn-on-source operations are coupled such that the joint sum is conserved across the cross-network state transition.
descriptions.system_theoretic: A conservation invariant on the JOINT network state. The state vocabulary is the cross-product of per-ledger states; the property asserts a relation `Σ_L supply_L(a) = issuedSupply(a)` is monotone-respected by every bridge protocol transition and by every per-ledger internal transition. It is single-trace at the joint level (one execution of the multi-network system) — NOT a hyperproperty — but it requires modelling the joint state rather than any single ledger in isolation.
descriptions.security: The economic backbone of any bridge or wrapped-asset design. Without cross-ledger consistency, a bridge bug or a desynchronization between the source-burn and destination-mint creates unbacked supply on the destination ledger or stranded supply on the source ledger — both are catastrophic. The 'wrapped-without-backing' inflation, and the 'burned-but-not-released' loss, are the canonical failures; the property is the negation of those failure modes.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Realized by paired mint/burn operations across ledgers, coordinated by a bridge relay protocol that proves to the destination chain that a source-chain burn (or lock) happened, and vice versa for redemption. The pairing must be atomic at the joint level: either both legs commit or neither. Violations live in: a destination-mint accepted without verifiable evidence of the paired source-burn / source-lock; a source-burn that releases without verifying the destination-burn for redemption; a relay protocol that can be replayed (re-presenting the same evidence to a destination chain twice); and a bridge upgrade or compromise that re-mints without burning.
descriptions.formal_verification: A 1-safety joint-state invariant. Establishing it requires (i) modelling the joint state of the participating ledgers, (ii) showing each per-ledger transition preserves Σ_L supply_L (only authorized bridge mints/burns change it, and they do so in paired fashion), and (iii) discharging the bridge-relay soundness — the relay's proof or attestation that a paired event happened on the other chain is itself a cryptographic / committee assumption. The within-ledger conservation half is discharged by BPO:0101 instantiated per ledger; the cross-ledger half is the new content here; the relay-soundness half is the load-bearing accepted-undischarged assumption.

formalization.signature: Ledgers L_1, ..., L_n; per-ledger supply supply_L : Asset × State_L → ℕ; issuedSupply : Asset × JointState → ℕ; bridge transitions br : Ledger × Ledger × Asset × ℕ × Evidence; joint state = (s_1, ..., s_n); relayVerify : Evidence × Ledger × Ledger → Bool.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Conservation invariant:  ∀ joint state (s_1, ..., s_n) reachable, ∀ a . Σ_L supply_L(a, s_L) = issuedSupply(a, (s_1, ..., s_n)).
Paired bridge transition:  ∀ br(L_src, L_dst, a, q, π) accepted: relayVerify(π, L_src, L_dst) = 1 ∧ supply_{L_src}(a) decreases by q at L_src ∧ supply_{L_dst}(a) increases by q at L_dst, in a paired joint transition.
No unpaired mint:  ∀ joint transition that changes supply_L(a) by +q : there exists a paired -q change at the source ledger evidenced by π with relayVerify(π) = 1.
Issuance:  issuedSupply changes only at the home ledger of the asset via the asset's native issuance / burn authorization.

temporal_logic.ltl: G( Σ_L supply_L(a) = issuedSupply(a) )   ∧   G( supplyChange(L_dst, a, +q) → ∃ π : relayVerify(π) ∧ pairedBurn(L_src, a, q, π) )
temporal_logic.fairness: Not required for the conservation invariant (pure safety). The compositional 'eventually-consistent representations' liveness claim (the destination mint eventually fires after the source burn) does need per-ledger consensus liveness (BPO:0080 per network) but is a separate property.

hoare.pre: joint state preserves Σ_L supply_L = issuedSupply
hoare.post: joint state still preserves Σ_L supply_L = issuedSupply

hoare.pre: relayVerify(π, L_src, L_dst) = 1 ∧ π attests pairedBurn(L_src, a, q)

formalization.state_machine: Joint automaton over n networks. Edges are either per-ledger transitions (which must preserve the joint sum by acting only on the home-ledger's authorized issuance/burn or by being internal moves with no supply effect) or paired bridge transitions (which atomically move q units from one ledger's representation to another's at the joint level). The property is that no edge breaks the joint sum identity.
formalization.type_theoretic: Bridge transfers are typed as joint-state-preserving moves of a single linear resource (a supply unit) between per-ledger representations. The destination-mint requires consuming a verifiable witness of the source-burn (a typed evidence object) which is itself a single-use, replay-resistant capability bound to the (source, destination, amount, nonce) tuple.
formalization.algebraic: (ℕ, +) commutative monoid per asset; supply_L is a per-ledger projection; Σ_L supply_L is the additive aggregate; bridge transitions are sum-preserving automorphisms of the joint state.

relationships.note: BPO:0101 is the within-ledger conservation invariant; BPO:0102 lifts the conservation discipline to the joint cross-ledger state, with bridge mints/burns as the cross-network analogue of internal flows.
A finalized source-burn followed by a destination-mint that respects the joint sum yields a final cross-ledger transfer; finality at the source is a precondition for the destination to safely mint.
Each participating ledger's consensus liveness is required for bridge protocols to eventually complete; the safety half does not require liveness but the compositional liveness claim does.
Replay-resistance: each bridge-relay evidence must be single-use across (src, dst, amount, nonce) so it cannot be replayed to mint twice on the destination.

attack_surface.pattern: the destination ledger's bridge contract mints without verifying source-burn evidence, or with a verifier that admits forged evidence
incident_refs: UNVERIFIED: historical bridge inflation incidents — verify before citing
attack_surface.notes: The relay-verifier is the load-bearing component; its soundness is the third assumption below.

attack_surface.pattern: the same source-burn evidence is presented twice to the destination, minting twice for one burn
attack_surface.notes: Composes with BPO:0092: evidence must carry a single-use nonce keyed to the destination so it cannot be re-presented.

attack_surface.pattern: the source ledger burns but the destination never mints due to a relay failure or a verifier rejection that doesn't surface to the source
attack_surface.notes: Composes with BPO:0091: a failed cross-ledger transfer must trigger a release on the source side (un-burn or compensating credit).

attack_surface.pattern: a committee-based relay's validator set rotates between the source-burn and destination-mint, accepting evidence from a now-deprecated set or rejecting evidence from the new one
attack_surface.notes: Validator-set commitment included in the evidence; rotation moves forward only and the destination tracks the evolution explicitly.

attack_surface.pattern: the destination accepts evidence rooted in a source state that later reorgs past its finality boundary, leaving the destination minted against a no-longer-final source-burn
attack_surface.notes: Composes with BPO:0090: only finalized source-burns may be presented as evidence.

metrics: Σ_L supply_L(a) − issuedSupply(a) per asset (target: always 0)
outstanding source-burns without matching destination-mints past the relay's expected bound (target: 0)
outstanding destination-mints not matched to a verifiable source-burn (target: 0)
invariant_checkpoints: Σ_L supply_L = issuedSupply at every joint-state snapshot
every bridge mint has a verifiable paired burn
every bridge burn has a paired mint or a compensating release
runtime_assertions: off-chain monitor periodically computes Σ_L supply_L and compares to issuedSupply; alert on drift
destination contract refuses to mint without verifying π

tools: Coq / Isabelle for the joint inductive argument
strategies.notes: Model the n-ledger joint state; show every transition preserves Σ_L supply_L = issuedSupply; bridge transitions discharge via the paired-mint-burn schema.

tools: Certora for the on-chain verifier contract
EasyCrypt for the underlying cryptographic reduction
strategies.notes: Prove the on-chain destination verifier accepts only evidence that genuinely attests a finalized source-burn under the relay's stated security model.

tools: off-chain watchers polling per-ledger supplies and the home ledger's issuedSupply
strategies.notes: Continuous monitoring of the joint sum identity; alerts on drift; cannot prove the invariant but catches violations quickly in production.

testability: any bridge transfer preserves Σ_L supply_L
replayed evidence rejected on the destination
reorg of a finalized source-burn does not retroactively justify a destination-mint
burn-without-mint triggers a release path on the source

runtime: destination contracts verify finalized-source evidence before minting
single-use evidence nonces keyed to (src, dst, amount)
static: bridge-verifier formally verified per the relay's security model
no path mints destination supply outside the verified bridge entry

assumptions.statement: Per-ledger conservation holds at each participating ledger; the within-ledger value measure is well-defined and conserved by internal transitions.
Each participating ledger's consensus is live under its own assumptions, so paired bridge transitions eventually complete.

The bridge relay is sound: the destination ledger accepts a relay evidence only when that evidence genuinely attests a finalized event on the source ledger (whether by ZK validity proof, light-client header verification, or honest-majority committee per the relay design). This is the load-bearing accepted-undischarged assumption: every cross-ledger inventory failure observed in production has bottomed out at relay-soundness, so it is named here as an open dependency rather than buried.

sources: bridge-design literature (Zamyatin et al. SoK on Communication across Distributed Ledgers, 2019)
provenance.notes: Authored as the formal version of DASCP C51-N's behavioural core for supply conservation across networks. The 'shared data' (non-supply data reconciliation) dimension of C51-N is intentionally not covered. The third assumption (relay soundness) is the explicit accepted-undischarged ledger entry the maintainer asked to keep visible: every cross-ledger inflation incident in the wild has bottomed out there.
